children: Cisco Systems, the networking and enterprise-security leader

, gained approximately 0.6% to $110.77 Tuesday morning after Splunk rolled out version 1.0 of Cisco AI POD for Splunk. The platform lets enterprises run Splunk's AI capabilities on Red Hat OpenShift within their own infrastructure, giving customers another route to deploy AI without pushing sensitive workloads into the public cloud. That matters for regulated industries where control over data and infrastructure can be just as important as raw computing power.

Cisco's fiscal fourth-quarter results showed just how quickly AI infrastructure is becoming a bigger piece of the story. Hyperscaler AI orders reached $4 billion in the quarter and $9.3 billion for fiscal 2026, while AI-infrastructure revenue came in at roughly $4 billion for the full year. Management expects that revenue to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027, which would represent an 87.5% year-over-year jump. Cisco is no longer simply waiting for traditional networking demand to improve; AI is becoming a measurable growth engine.

The valuation already reflects plenty of enthusiasm. At $110.765, Cisco trades 48.48% above the GuruFocus GF Value estimate of $74.60, suggesting investors are paying a substantial premium for the company's AI and networking growth potential. Splunk gives Cisco another way to monetize the AI buildout beyond switches and hyperscaler infrastructure, but the next test is execution: converting deployments into meaningful recurring software revenue while delivering the aggressive AI-infrastructure growth already embedded in expectations.

title: Cisco Gains as Its $7.5 Billion AI Target Moves On-Premises
